Author: IBM
Summary:
Yes, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is coming. It’s a wide-ranging regulation that will have new requirements including heightened protection for personal data. The GDPR applies to the processing of personal data by all organizations located in the European Union (EU) and, in addition, to all organizations located outside the EU that are processing personal data of individuals that are in the EU, where such processing is related to the offering of goods and services to individuals in the EU or the monitoring of their behavior taking place in the EU (e.g. via tracking technology). This applies to living individuals on EU soil, both citizens and non citizens alike. A surprising number of company leaders seem to be taking a wait-and-see approach to GDPR, and given the scope of the regulation, that’s understandable --- but it may not be wise.

That is because GDPR isn’t just a toothless suggestion, but a serious regulation that goes into effect as of May 25, 2018. And so, ready or not, it really is time to start getting your personal data in shape and putting your organization on a GDPR diet. But fear not! You do not have to run a GDPR marathon right out of the gate. You can get started by taking small steps that will help you get results - without going on a crash diet.

Join this webcast and use the following information, so that you can put together your own GDPR diet:

• Basic concepts you need to know about GDPR to get organized
• Small steps that can help you get started making progress toward your GDPR goals
• Baby step 1: Stop drinking soda to start making progress (aka - consider data encryption to help jump start your diet)
• Baby step 2: Start walking to burn more calories (aka - consider data classification to help continue your momentum)
• Baby step 3: Hit the weights! (aka - consider data access monitoring to help you achieve the next level on your diet)

Get started preparing for GDPR!

For further information on the end to end Assessment, Process, Policy and Solution capabilities IBM offers for all clients GDPR Programs, see our Pathways Point of View whitepaper and further resources at ibm.com/gdpr
Title: The GDPR diet: Small steps to help you get results

Author: IBM
Summary:
Roles were invented to make the provisioning and deprovisioning of users easier. And they worked; they still do. The ability to give a new user all (or most) of the access needed to perform a job role is leaps and bounds better than manually provisioning individual users for their specific duties on an ad-hoc basis.

The challenge comes from the recent explosion in the numbers and types of business roles. Organizations became so focused on having the perfect role for every user group that even slight variations in a person’s profile or access needs would lead to the creation of an entirely separate role. The problem was: If the IT-enabled constraints that controlled user entitlements—the permissions they are granted to take action—were linked only to general titles, the more specialized roles might go overlooked, with no controls at all.

Register to read on and learn how IBM Security Identity Governance and Intelligence gives you better control over access with visibility into entitlements - not just roles.
Title: For better access governance, look beyond roles to entitlements

While many of these jobs will be in the manufacturing sector, some companies are testing robots’ ability to interact customers and support customer needs.

• Constantly monitoring data
• Encrypting data, regardless of its location
• Managing encryption keys throughout the data life cycle
• Monitoring encryption keys

Join this webcast to learn more about the importance of data encryption and dig into these four best practices, to learn how you can apply these best practices to your Cloud environments.

Summary: Internet Protocol (IP) telephony is increasingly replacing traditional PBX technologies at all types and sizes of companies. Summary:
Integrating business eCommerce with enterprise resource planning (ERP) software is a growing trend recently. If a business is looking to do this, it needs to keep in mind that not all ERP vendors offer the features needed to successfully implement.

Luckily, this side-by-side comparison guide compares the top 10 ERP for eCommerce solutions and note-worthy feature sets such as storefront management, order fulfillment, payment processing, and much more.

Summary: Technology escaped the data center and now threads through every corner of your business. Users now demand instant gratification for every data request 24x7. To keep up with these demands and fuel growth, build on the secure and reliable data foundation of DB2®.

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Congratulations! You got the sale and closed the deal, thus gaining a new customer. The sales-cycle doesn’t end there. Acquiring new clients is great, but keeping the ones you have is just as (or even more) important. Having a Customer Relationship Management system (CRM) that helps deal with customer inquiries, problems, and solutions is important for any company that views customer service as the crux of their business model.

In this guide, you will learn about the top CRM vendors that provide features and tools to help companies optimize their customer service. Many include key features such as real time escalation of cases, customizable workflow, and analytics to track and group problem areas.
Title: CRM for Customer Service Comparison Guide

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Docking stations have been around for many years in a variety of forms, but have followed a particular evolution path when it comes to communications. Unless you have stayed current with this space, you may associate docking stations with passive devices that do little more than charge your computer or smartphone. With the advent of wireless broadband and affordable, high-powered mobile devices, docking stations have another role to play in a business environment. Instead of focusing on keeping devices charged and providing a better experience for music and videos, IP docking stations can enhance productivity in entirely new ways.

This guide has been prepared to help you understand the opportunity and determine both if and how today’s docking stations can help you get the most out of the devices your employees are increasingly relying on. Here we outline five key considerations you need to address to make the right decisions whether you see these docking stations as either an enabler for VoIP, or for the broader benefits that come with Unified Communications.
Title: IP Phone Docking Guide White Paper

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Unified Communications is a big step up from VoIP, and has more complexity in terms of having a successful deployment. Technology and network-related issues are part of why, but there is another dimension that our research indicates is not well understood. This guide has been prepared to help you navigate through the subtle challenges of driving adoption and gaining buy-in for UC. IT must take full ownership of the UC opportunity, while providing practical strategies for each audience. While IT and vendors may speak the same language about UC, management does not, and here you will learn what is really important for getting them to adopt UC.

To get management truly invested, IT needs to address a series of challenges that will position UC in the best light. This guide will teach you about these five key challenges for IT to build their case around.
Title: Driving UC Adoption in your Business

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary: The term “social CRM” carries two very different meanings for businesses. On the one hand, social CRM can refer to customer relationship management systems that track social media campaigns and engagement. On the other, social CRM systems can be considered those that use familiar features of social networking to facilitate collaboration and communication across and within business units. The first is increasingly critical for successful marketing and sales; the second is becoming indispensable for organizations looking to involve a variety of stakeholders in customer-centered sales cycles. This paper explores both facets of social CRM and explains how businesses can benefit from their implementations.
Title: Why CRM is Important to Business

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Chances are that telephony has been the center of your communications universe for as long as you can remember. You’re not alone, and this still holds true for the vast majority of small-to-medium businesses, and even large enterprises. However, even with just a bit of research, it’s easy to see that lots of changes are underway.

More than ever, communications is a competitive driver, and to take advantage, you need a vision that goes beyond telecom. The landscape is much broader today, and this primer will prepare you with practical overview of communications technologies and essentials you’ll need to successfully bring them into your business. Use this checklist analysis of the five essentials you need to address in order to grow beyond conventional telephony.
Title: 5 Essentials for Success to Grow Beyond Telecom

Summary:

But marketers aren’t the only ones discovering the inherent value of ‘likes’ and hashtags. More and more contact centers are embracing social media as a powerful tool for addressing customer concerns and empowering agents.

More than 63 percent of businesses may use at least one UC app, according to Nemertes Research, but the social etiquette side has not caught up with adoption.

So listen up: Don’t be a UC noob. Here are seven of the most common UC etiquette mistakes. Don’t make these mistakes.

Summary:

The difference between the promise and the reality of big data currently presents a sizeable competitive advantage for businesses that seize the opportunity, especially when it comes to ERP.

From sales forecasting and scheduling to predictive maintenance and enhanced quality control, big data can improve ERP in many ways. Here are seven of the most important areas where big data helps ERP.

Summary:
Customer relationship management is fundamentally about managing and maximizing a company’s interaction with the people who buy its products, influence its markets, and support its operations. With social media now playing such a large role in the lives of just about everyone, it reasons that CRM also must be social.

The social component of CRM typically includes enhanced customer profiles, social listening, segment analysis, social selling and social marketing, among other benefits. With its rise, CRM is changing from department-specific to encompass all areas of a business. With that in mind, here are five tips for better using your social CRM system.
Title: Five Tips for Better Social CRM

Summary:

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Are you a small to mid-sized business with an expensive to maintain, dated legacy phone system? Not sure what kind of phone system you have, or exactly what it does? That’s okay! As long as you realize that every organization needs telephony, you’re starting in the right direction.

Author: IBM
Summary:
The good news is that enterprise search has been around for decades and usually does an adequate job. The bad news is that the adequate job only provides lists of search results and a way to navigate and review the results. Finding documents that contain certain keywords? Check. Searching relational databases? Check. Coordinating search results from multiple internal data stores? Check. Searching content outside the company, such as premium information services? Check. Providing deep content analytics with mature supporting tools? Providing unified information applications, and collaboration? Providing advanced cognitive capabilities? Those capabilities remain out of reach for the majority of players in the enterprise search arena.

With Watson Explorer, you can keep enterprise search as the foundation and transform search into Cognitive Exploration. Leveraging technological advances such as deep search and exploration, advanced content analytics, and cognitive capabilities, IBM Watson Explorer provides a unified view of the information you need, combining data from multiple internal silos and a variety of outside datasets including social media. Stop limiting your search to traditional data sources in the new, non-traditional data world.

Summary:
Data streams are continuous, always on and never ceasing. Those in the telecommunications industry, are often overwhelmed with data streams spewing from mobile devices. But, continuous, complete and connected streaming environments have the potential to make this data available for analyst and data scientists. The results can be significant for business stakeholders. Results include: increased customer satisfaction, maximized asset utilization and proactive retention the most profitable customers. IBM Streams enables continuous processing of data streams.

Join us to explore three client examples around: CRM mediation, intelligent campaigns and next best action. Others reduces new campaign launch time by more than 80%. Bring your questions and tough challenges around processing continuous data streams.

Arvind Sathi,
World Wide Communication Sector Architect for IBM Analytics Division

Kevin Foster,
IBM Big Data Solutions Architect

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
At face value, VoIP is easy to understand, especially if your primary driver is cost savings. However, there is more than meets the eye to VoIP. With so many VoIP services and solutions to choose from, as well as embarking on a foundational shift away from legacy telephony, this is a scenario where proper preparation pays off.

We are well-versed in the challenges for new VoIP adopters and recognize that a major knowledge gap still exists. To that end, this guide has been prepared and focuses on five key factors you may not have yet considered that will have a major impact on your VoIP implementation.
Title: 5 Things to Know Before Implementing VoIP

Author: Genesys
Summary:
As mid-size companies look for a competitive edge in an increasingly global marketplace, one approach that can deliver measurable results is to integrate customer relationship management (CRM) tools with contact center applications and services for a deep 360-degree view of the customer, tracking every interaction to ensure an optimal customer experience.

Frost & Sullivan research shows that today, only about one-third of contact centers are fully integrated, while the largest proportion is mostly integrated. But by 2016, 54% of surveyed organizations expect to be fully integrated (a 64% growth rate over the two-year period). This will pave the way for more-advanced integration between the contact center itself and other back-office systems, most notably CRM platforms—since the ability to deliver a consistent and seamless customer experience is a high priority for 49% of surveyed contact center decision-makers, a number expected to rise even more (15%) by 2016.

Read this paper to get a high-level view of the modern contact center; learn about the rapidly changing needs and expectations of customers today; see details of the benefits of integrating CRM and contact center systems, especially for mid-size organizations; and get an outline of best practices for success.
Title: Frost & Sullivan—When CRM Meets the Contact Center

Author: Genesys
Summary:
The complexity of today’s contact center is at an all-time high with a future indicating more channels to manage, increased customer expectations to fulfill, and a need for a frontline workforce that is, by no means, “entry level”. That doesn’t mean providing an effortless customer experience is impossible, it just means that you need to be ready to handle whatever comes your way. Creating an effortless customer experience requires insider knowledge from three key stakeholders:

  • The Customer
  • The Agent
  • The Organization
Fortunately for you, we’ve received insider secrets from each of them on what organizational leaders can do, right now, to remove three common roadblocks to an effortless customer experience. In this whitepaper, you’ll receive tips for solving these problems and putting an effortless customer experience within your reach. From the customer’s core expectations, to the right metrics for the organization to measure, to the systems and processes that agents need for success, you’ll have the core components required for lowering customer effort and elevating the overall customer experience.

Author: Genesys
Summary:

For mid-sized companies, the burden of providing superior customer service is even greater. Mid-size companies represent the healthiest sector of the economy, responsible for almost half of global job growth. While these growing enterprises are driving much of the market’s innovation, they must remain nimble in how they operate, and be very responsive to customer needs. They are often new entrants to a market or need to compete against much larger competitors. The difference between success and failure is often in the delivery of a superior customer experience.

A sophisticated CRM system can deliver enormous benefits, from increasing customer satisfaction and generating sales leads to boosting profits and slashing operating costs. A CRM system works by gathering information from multiple data sources and storing it in a centralized location. Once these sales leads and consumer data sets are integrated, this information is then analyzed to enable tailored marketing campaigns, superior customer service and improved decision support. Yet the success of a CRM strategy doesn’t hinge on fancy features but rather how quickly employees embrace the solution. For starters, many organizations are unaware of the powerful impact a CRM system can have on the bottom line. Another hindrance to widespread CRM adoption is a failure to properly customize a solution for an organization’s unique needs.

Download this whitepaper to learn why leaders need to take the time to consider what business problems they want CRM to address, what business processes CRM will impact and how the system will grow with the company’s needs. Summary:
Integrating business eCommerce with enterprise resource planning (ERP) software is a growing trend recently. If a business is looking to do this, it needs to keep in mind that not all ERP vendors offer the features needed to successfully implement.

Luckily, this side-by-side comparison guide compares the top 10 ERP for eCommerce solutions and note-worthy feature sets such as storefront management, order fulfillment, payment processing, and much more.
Title: ERP for eCommerce Comparison Guide

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
These days, a lot of employees work away remotely. The most visible of them are those who are traveling for business, but there are also those who work from home or in small and/or remote branch offices. Even small companies can have overseas employees, and many of them may switch among any combination of these work situations at different times. In any case, all represent different types of mobile workers and cloud VoIP providers offer a variety of ways to keep such workers connected.

Download this guide to have more insight on six cloud VoIP providers that offer various mobility capabilities.
Title: VoIP Mobility Buyer's Guide

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Contact centers benefit any company whose employees spend a lot of time talking with customers on the phone, whether through incoming sales or service calls or through outgoing sales calls; therefore, this helps companies deal with large numbers of customers more effectively. Until cloud VoIP came along, contact centers were available only to the largest companies with hundreds of agents. Now the same capabilities are available to companies of every size.

This Buyer's Guide assesses six cloud contact center VoIP providers that offer significant contact center capabilities and features. If you're looking to run a formal or de facto call center, you will likely find one among these that will fit your needs.
Title: Cloud VoIP Contact Centers Buyer's Guide

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
At times, doing business requires being on top of mobility and its applications. With more and more workers using bring your own devices (BYOD), managing mobile applications is an important aspect of overall business functionality. That’s where mobile application management (MAM) software steps in to aid organizations with this task.

This guide compares the top 10 MAM solutions and key features such as security enforcement, performance monitoring, usage tracking and more.
Title: Mobile Application Mangement (MAM) Comparison Guide

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
This glossary provides a useful list of common terms and their definitions to help nontechnical business users familiarize themselves with Voice over IP (VoIP), also known as Internet telephony.

If you find yourself responsible for procuring a new VoIP system or commenting on a potential contract, you will find many of the terms here mentioned during technical conversations when determining the requirements of a project and working through the quotation process.
Title: The Business User's Glossary to VoIP

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Because VoIP by definition operates over IP networks, it is relatively easy to integrate with other IP-based communication methods.

A product category called unified communications, or UC, has emerged that makes VoIP even more useful and flexible, by integrating it with a number of such methods. This guide assesses six cloud UC providers. Each of them defines UC in a way that reflects its overall product line. In keeping with the flexibility that VoIP and IP technology in general make possible, the providers target a broad variety of customer needs and sizes.
Title: Cloud VoIP Unified Communications Buyer's Guide

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Still running on a legacy analog system? Or how about that old PBX that isn’t as reliable as it was back when it was purchased in the 80s? Perhaps it’s time to upgrade your business phone solution. A lot of businesses look at Voice over IP (VoIP) telephony due to its cost savings and excess of features that any company of any size can utilize.

The VoIP industry is very competitive, and it can be difficult for an organization to choose a system to meet its needs. Download this free side-by-side comparison guide that highlights the top 10 vendors and their feature offerings. Also get the inside scoop on which solutions work best for which businesses.
Title: Business VoIP Comparison Guide

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Small to mid-size business can enjoy big business features from cloud VoIP solutions with little to no upfront spending. Other benefits include ease of use, minimal to no IT pros managing the system, scalability, and much more.

Ziff Davis contributing writer Robert Poe researched different vendors and feature sets that are noteworthy when it comes to purchasing a SMB phone system, so you don’t have to. This guide is also designed to put all the information in one spot, where it can be easily referenced when it’s time to buy.
Title: Cloud VoIP SMB Phone Systems

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
The conventional wisdom is that cloud VoIP is suitable for smaller companies, and it is. But cloud VoIP also has attractions for larger companies. In particular, the flexibility it offers can be especially appealing for organizations with large, geographically dispersed work forces. Accordingly, a number of providers are specifically targeting enterprise customers, offering the same capabilities as high-end premises systems.

This guide introduces six cloud VoIP providers with offerings that enterprises may find appealing. As with other cloud VoIP products, they package and sell different combinations of features in a variety of ways. For enterprises looking to boost their communication capabilities, they are worth looking at.
Title: Cloud VoIP Enterprise Phone System Buyer's Guide

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
According to the McKinsey Global Institute, about 72 percent of companies use some form of social technology within the organization. The problem is few of those companies are realizing the full value of social tools. When done well, social technologies have the potential to increase the productivity of interaction works by about 20–25 percent. So, what are the best tools to implement?

Before examining the answer to that question, it might be good to explore the idea of integrating social capabilities into an organization. It doesn’t mean connecting the company to Facebook or announcing every decision on Twitter. Organizational social tools can be both public and private but usually consist of a suite of apps or capabilities that a solution vendor provides. Social enterprise resource planning (ERP) tools are either integrated into the ERP application or are available as premium add-on apps.

This side-by-side comparison guide highlights the top 10 vendors that provide social tools for ERP applications such as communication monitoring, built-in security, internal social networks and more.

Source: "Social ERP Tools: What Works, What Doesn't?" by Jerri Ledford
Title: Social Tools for ERP Applications Comparison Guide

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
In this white paper, learn more about the many approaches an organization can take when it comes to ERP implementation, the main three being:

  • Big bang rollout
  • Phased rollout
  • Parallel adoption
This paper also discusses the advantages and disadvantages of each mentioned implementation strategy, with the main takeaway being there is no one-size-fits-all when it comes to implementing an ERP system and to choose the best strategy for your particular business.
Title: ERP Implementation Strategies

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
What do enterprise resource planning (ERP), NFL playoffs commercials, and the movie Fight Club have in common? In “Right-sizing ERP for SMBs,” Ziff Davis writer and Studio B analyst Shelton Hill correlates the above mentioned to cloud-based ERP solutions for SMBs.

You will also learn that by having a customizable, flexible, and scalable cloud ERP solution in place, you can successfully execute key business processes that are essential to your organization.
Title: Right-sizing ERP for SMBs

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary: In this white paper, Ziff Davis contributing writer and studio B analyst Anthony Ortega lays out the “need to know” for small businesses who have heard of the term enterprise resource planning (ERP), but don’t fully have a grasp on it, much less think of it as any benefit to their small operation. Fortunately, there are a good number of benefits ERP can bring, and despite popular belief that ERP systems are too expensive, we are now in an era where it can be affordable as long as a company properly budgets according to its individual business needs.
Title: Understanding Small Business ERP

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Whether you're just starting out a business venture on your own, or have been in business for years, customer relationship management (CRM) plays a vital role in organizations of all shapes and sizes. CRM technology is rapidly growing, and with thanks to the Internet of Things (IoT), it is easier to tie everything together, keep track of business processes as well as your customers.

This white paper discusses the latest CRM features that satisfy KPIs, ways to gather customer data in order to market to them correctly, and when as well as how to take CRM to the cloud.

Topics discussed to help you get the most out of today’s CRM systems include:
  • Apples to Apples: What All CRM Solutions Need to Do Well
  • How to Leverage Your Customer Database for Marketing Success
  • SaaS-ifying CRM and the Resources Supporting It
Title: Getting the Most Out of CRM

Author: ZD B2B A
Summary:
Companies looking to implement an up-to-date, innovative enterprise resource planning (ERP) system must be prepared to sift through a complicated vendor landscape. Today's executives must choose from a staggering number of ERP solutions, ranging from on-premise, feature-rich systems to newer, lesser-known cloud-based alternatives. The trick is making a purchasing decision that meets an organization's budgetary, operational and business processing requirements.

So how can a company in the market for an ERP solution make a proper purchasing decision? This ERP buyer's guide outlines the pros and cons of various delivery models, advises on how to select a solution for the future and discusses some lesser-known roadblocks to a successful ERP implementation.
Title: ERP: The Buyer's Guide

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
The health care industry looks at customer relationship management (CRM) as a way to facilitate the means of tracking where patients come from to where they need to go since this is not only a good business practice, but also a medical necessity.

This comparison guide updated for 2016, provides side-by-side comparisons of top industry CRM solutions for health care organizations as well as features tailored for small family practices, to large hospitals with locations across the country.
Title: CRM for Healthcare Comparison Guide

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary: In this white paper, Ziff Davis contributing writer Cindy Waxer along with Paul Rebenstein, leader of talent solutions and strategies at Aon Hewitt, explain more in depth about why performance management tools aren’t enough when it comes to measuring your KPIs-It's about your employee's performance as a team that contributes to overall team success. Also mentioned are a few key points on how to attract top talent and how to keep them working for you.
Title: Talent Management: What You Need to Know to Ensure Top Performers, Team Success, and Retention

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Businesses tend to be faced with deciding whether to implement a customer relationship management (CRM) or an enterprise resource planning (ERP) solution when it comes to what is best for managing both the customer and large amounts of company data. What most companies rarely realize is that both are needed to be as economical as possible because without the automated and fluid processes ERP provides, a CRM can only contain the various and (often) large amounts of data with limited efficiency.

So when it comes to the sales force, integrating ERP and CRM helps improves forecasting and automation, vendor relationships, and identifying and growing profitable relationships. This side-by-side comparison guide highlights the top vendors in the industry who provide these key features and more.
Title: ERP CRM Sales Integration Solutions Comparison Guide

Author: IBM
Summary:
Data centers are growing at a fast pace and operators are struggling with many challenges such as whether to increase on-premises compute capacity, adopt public cloud infrastructure, or turn to other managed services to meet their increasing needs.

In this survey report, Ziff Davis asked 284 IT decision-makers to rate three different focus areas in enterprise data centers, and also provided a forum for open-ended responses in order to take a snapshot of the current priorities, challenges, and business alignment goals in IT today.
Title: Strategic IT Survey Results: Data Center Services

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Customer relationship management (CRM) software is praised in the marketplace as the next best thing in sales and marketing intelligence solutions.

Download "Top Five Best and Worst CRM Practices," in order to discover that the CRM software, in and of itself, is typically not the source when good and/or poor results occur.
Title: Top Five Best and Worst CRM Practices

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Today’s business settings has companies constantly looking for ways to manage large amounts of data, analyze it, and present it in an organized way. This needs to be done in order to help paint a clear picture of the business life cycle to ensure efficiency.

Luckily, enterprise resource planning (ERP) performance solutions are able to handle a broad range of information, and in this side-by-side comparison guide updated for 2016 you will learn more about features that aid your organization’s data analysis and reporting such as compliance management, demand forecasting, and inventory valuation.
Title: ERP Performance Management and BI Comparison Guide

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
In the past, enterprise resource planning (ERP) and supply chain management (SCM) were difficult to integrate. It wasn’t until recent advancements that made integration of the two a bit more conceivable. Today, companies are now looking at both as “must haves” in order to operate at optimal efficiency and are also observing advantages such as improved forecasting accuracy, reduced inventory levels, and even improved customer service.

This 10x10 comparison guide updated for 2016 highlights the top ERP vendors and features tailored to helping organizations get a tighter control on the supply chain.
Title: ERP Supply Chain Comparison Guide

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Finding good people to employ is a goal all businesses want to achieve. Once obtaining those star employees, seeking easier ways to organize, develop, and manage your workforce can be accomplished using enterprise resource planning (ERP) human resources modules.

In this recently updated comparison guide, we’ve listed the top vendors that offer ERP HR solutions that assist companies with automating processes such as employee payroll, benefits, and evaluations.
Title: ERP Human Resources Comparison Guide

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Enterprise resource planning (ERP) software modules are tailored to aid in business-specific needs. When it comes to manufacturing and distribution companies, the need to manage the supply chain is important, especially since supply and demand can be fickle. In order for manufacturers to closely ensure business processes run as smooth as possible, an ERP manufacturing module helps automate functions such as quality control, order accuracy, and communication between supplier and distributor.

In this updated comparison guide for 2016, you will learn about the top ERP solutions including specific manufacturing module features offered such as inventory management, material requirements planning, bar coding and much more.
Title: ERP for Manufacturing Comparison Guide

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Customer relationship management (CRM) solutions help small and midsize businesses manage the myriad of ways it interacts with customers—from marketing to customers, to improving customer support.

As a matter of fact, companies of all sizes rely on it to capture new customers and retain current ones, which is reason enough to invest in the technology. In this checklist, we will give you six reasons why you should convince management to integrate a CRM solution for your business ASAP.
Title: 6 Ways to Sell Management on CRM

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Having an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) finance module is a way for a company to organize its financials as well as meet its business objectives in the most efficient way. Most solutions aid in generating general ledgers, balance sheets, expense tracking, and quarterly financial statements.

In this updated 2016 guide, you will learn more about the top 10 ERP vendors who offer finance modules and important features to consider before implementing such as ease of customization to, user range, financing options.

They also need to be able to do more with less -- more computing power with fewer servers, smaller teams and leaner budgets.

Topics covered include Linux servers, IBM Power Systems, SAP applications and business systems, a real-world case study showcasing the benefits of replacing underperforming servers, Big Data, techniques for better server management and more. Download this exclusive IT Managers' Journal and learn how to get more out of your data centers today.

Summary: Cloud computing models offer a new approach for IT organizations to deliver business services to end users. It is a technology model that provides both flexible IT deployments and dynamic business agility. The model offers capacity on a pay-as-you-go basis. That is, it provides a method of freeing and uniting computing capacity that had been isolated within business units. It makes system resources accessible to applications that span the entire organization. At its full potential, cloud computing can accelerate business innovation and transformation.
Title: Best Practices for Cloud Computing Adoption

Summary:
The hodgepodge of communication modes, applications and devices can make it challenging for people to connect properly. Unified communications attempts to tackle this challenge by letting ccompanies manage voice mail, faxes, email and video from a single inbox using a single set of management controls. Disparate communication systems are linked together, allowing users to interact independent of device or media.

In this whitepaper, contributing Ziff Davis analyst Cindy Waxer breaks down unified communications by defining it, explaining how it works, ROI, UC challenges in an organization, and questions IT leaders need to ask before deployment.
Title: Unified Communications: The Layman's Guide

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Customer relationship management systems have come a long way from being nothing more than high-tech Rolodexes. Once known for storing reams upon reams of contact information such as customer names and addresses, today's CRM technologies deliver high-tech analytics capabilities, highly personalized communications and collaborative platforms. Together, these cutting-edge features aim to recapture the customer service once provided by local mom-and-pop shops.

This white paper will introduce readers to a CRM system's key benefits and modules, as well as explore the five trends shaping the technology's future.
Title: Introduction to Customer Relationship Mangement

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Contact Centers are exactly what the name implies: A place where customers can get ahold of an organization. They’re also an important aspect for businesses to easily communicate with customers and provide great service.

This comparison guide provides the top 10 providers and highlights key features to look for when considering a hosted solution for your business call center.

Summary: This Frost & Sullivan report provides insight on the importance of infrastructure in optimizing analytics deployment and the key advantages derived by implementing IBM analytics infrastructure solutions. Title: Smarter Analytics for Insurers - Unlevel the Playing Field with Intelligent Infrastructures

Summary: This white paper shows how IBM Smarter Storage provides customers with an ideal, proven platform for cloud computing. Learn about IBM's differentiated storage portfolio, including XIV, Scale Out NAS (SONAS), SAN Volume Controller (SVC), Tivoli Storage Manager (TSM), Tivoli Storage Productivity Center (TPC), and SmartCloud solutions.
Title: IDC: Eliminate Shortcomings in Your Cloud Architecture with Smarter Storage

Author: IBM
Summary:
Business processes and supporting IT infrastructure are changing. We're in the early stages of the 3rd Platform of computing, in which Big Data, cloud computing, mobile, and social technologies are fundamentally transforming the business and IT landscape. And as 3rd Platform technologies increasingly become mission-critical, they require an infrastructure with features and capabilities to support other resource-intensive, mission-critical workloads such as OLTP, business applications, and data warehouses.

The IBM POWER platform is designed to address the needs of both current mission-critical workloads and 3rd platform workloads. Power Systems can encompass the scalability and multi-tenancy needs of the 3rd Platform – in particular Big Data analytics and cloud. With its history of investment and community innovation plus advances in the latest generation of POWER technology, IBM Power is positioned as an excellent choice for datacenter infrastructure, well into the era of the 3rd Platform. This IDC White Paper explores these topics and others and offers their view opportunities and challenges for Power as it helps integrate and support the demands of traditional business applications and new, 3rd platform applications.
Title: IDC: IBM's Innovations for the Virtualization, Multi-tenancy, and Cloud Demands of the 3rd Platform

Author: IBM
Summary:
Most organizations today are either considering or have already adopted at least one Cloud service. Due to its many benefits, such as speed, flexibility and cost effectiveness, SaaS is the fastest growing sector in today's software industry. But in reality, while companies are quickly reaching for the Cloud, many will continue to use traditional on-premise applications and systems.

Such hybrid enterprise IT environments have become the norm as they allow organizations to pick and choose the right combination of infrastructure, platform and software as a service to make the most of their Cloud investments. Hybrid cloud environments are growing in popularity and are quickly embedded into a growing number of mission critical systems, but to leverage their undisputable benefits, significant integration challenges must first be dealt with.

As a technology leader, IBM has been leading and continues to lead in this hybrid integration space with IBM WebSphere Cast Iron Cloud Integration. Listen to this session to uncover how IBM can help customers quickly meet their cloud integration requirements.
Title: Hybrid cloud integration in just days

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
If you are considering Unified Communications now, chances are you are already using VoIP, and presumably that has been meeting your expectations. Whereas VoIP is a singular mode of communication, UC covers multiple modes and will accommodate new ones as they come along. This is but one example of how UC is different than VoIP, and we have prepared this guide to further explain the various differences that make the decision-making process so difficult.

Ziff Davis has published other guides that explain why and how UC is good for your business, and presuming you have come to that conclusion, “Making Sense of Unified Communications - Five Decision-Making Strategies” should prove very timely. You will also learn about five key trends on the current state of UC, along with five strategies for IT to make the right choices.
Title: Making Sense of Unified Communications - Five Decision-Making Strategies

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Once you've reached a point to retire your legacy phone system and move towards a voice over internet protocol (VoIP) system, determining how you migrate to and from becomes the next priority. While you don't need to know every aspect of this migration from the outset, you certainly need an overall roadmap, not only for your own planning, but also to provide management both comfort and confidence in moving to VoIP now.

The success factors outlined in "Five Signs You Need a VoIP Phone System" should be adequate for both needs, and by addressing these, the risks associated with VoIP will be minimized to the point where you'll be wondering why you didn’t do this sooner.
Title: Migrating Your Business to VoIP – Five Key Success Factors

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Legacy telecom vendors have little incentive to transition you to voice over internet protocol (VoIP), and as long as the phone system is working, you’ll need to discover those reasons yourself.

This guide has drawn from carefully compiled research about how SMBs think about phone systems and the triggers that lead to making a change. From this, we have identified five such reasons that tell you the time is right for a VoIP phone system.
Title: Five Signs You Need a VoIP Phone System

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Phone systems are the communications lifeblood of all businesses, but can be limiting in several ways. This is certainly true for legacy telephony, where phone systems were not just expensive but inflexible. They did a great job with telephony service, but created a centralized environment that posed challenges for businesses looking to expand beyond their four walls.

This guide explains how hosted voice over internet protocol (VoIP) system brings greater flexibility for small businesses and frees them from the limitations imposed by legacy telephony. These freedoms, however, bring business-level implications, which are also explored in order to give this guide a balanced perspective.
Title: Decentralize Your Business Operations with Hosted VoIP Phone Systems

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
VoIP has taken a different evolutionary path than legacy system, and while the services have many basic equivalencies, the value propositions diverge beyond that. The underlying technologies are complex, but you don’t need to go that deep to understand the nature of VoIP and how it can do things that legacy telephony cannot. VoIP is the product of a different era for communications technology and has the benefit of many innovations that did not exist when the PSTN was developed.

For that reason, VoIP offers value beyond everyday telephony, and if that is important in your decision-making process, this primer will be very relevant. Based on our ongoing research, five basic elements of VoIP’s technology have been identified for analysis, and we believe these will greatly strengthen your understanding as to both how and why VoIP will be good for your business.
Title: VoIP Primer-5 Technology Basics that Add Value for Businesses

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) is, in short, management software for your business. It helps run all aspects from customer data, accounting, human resources, manufacturing, etc. An organization can also integrate various applications dedicated to a specific business function as well as automate back office tasks.

If you are new to ERP and looking to see what options are available in market, this guide will help you start with the basics. It highlights the top ten solutions and the main features you should be looking at when considering integrating ERP.

This guide has been prepared to make the case for premise-based VoIP. It analyzes five key reasons for choosing this option, which is based on our ongoing industry research, and collectively we believe it provides a solid foundation to support your decision for implementing premise-based VoIP.
Title: 5 Reasons to Deploy a Premise-Based VoIP System

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
When emergencies happen, our first instinct is often to call 911. In the U.S., this has long been a universal service – at least in our homes. Today, that service is known as E911, and whether you know that or not, most people don’t give much thought as to how it works. This is particularly problematic for businesses since most environments do not fully or properly support E911. Not only are the technologies and solutions largely inadequate, but in most states, E911 support for businesses is not mandatory.

This guide has been prepared to draw from industry-based research and distill the current state of business E911 for decision-makers. We have identified five need-to-know realities that all businesses must address, and believe this will provide a solid basis for you to determine a go-forward plan for E911.
Title: Five Things You Must Know About E911

Author: IBM
Summary: A data breach, probings, hackers… you need to protect your your critical IT information. What these real-life examples have in common is that perpetrators can attack companies through their IT systems. Read how trusted computing from IBM PureFlex System can help secure your systems against emerging threats.
Title: Protect Your IT System with Next Generation Security

Author: IBM
Summary: Companies worldwide are embracing private clouds, not only because they support new, highly efficient and secure data solutions, but also to drive new competitive organizational strategies. This white paper provides an assessment of the business value of implementing IBM SmartCloud Entry for Power Systems versus comparable private cloud solutions from VMware on Intel. It discusses the benefits of private cloud solutions, including reduced labor and hardware/software costs, ease of implementation and adoption, scalability, organizational flexibility, security, improved efficiency, as well as allocation of and access to IT resources.
Title: Edison Group - The Business and Economic Advantages of SmartCloud Entry for Power Systems

Author: IBM
Summary: Watson’s success in the Jeopardy! challenge was inspiring, but the business impact of optimized systems design is just beginning. With smarter analytics solutions optimized on IBM Power Systems, you can put Watson's technology to work.
Title: Make Better Decisions Faster with Business Analytics on IBM Power Systems

Author: IBM
Summary: Get the most information from your data. Business has never been faster and is increasingly dependent on the timely analysis of large volumes of data for strategic and operational decisions. As executives come to rely on advanced analytics, the importance of a robust IT infrastructure cannot be overstated. Data comes from everywhere; make sure you get it in time, every time.
Title: An Executive Guide to Analytics Infrastructure: Imperatives for Advanced Analytics

Author: IBM
Summary: This paper shows how the new IBM systems with X6 technology were designed to take clients to a new frontier of x86 computing. These new X6 systems are ideal platforms for meeting business-critical demands with data base, business analytics, virtualization and ERP applications.
Title: IDC: Enterprise Workloads on the IBM X6 Portfolio - Driving Business Advantages

Author: IBM
Summary: In this Advisory, Clabby Analytics looks more closely at the importance of implementing an integrated infrastructure — and its relationship to business analytics. The paper will examine the business analytics workloads, discuss how these workloads put different demands on the underlying systems and infrastructure, and provide guidance designing an integrated business analytics environment that will provide organizations with high performance, resiliency, and a scalable growth path.
Title: Business Analytics Buying Criteria: The Three Maxims

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
For most Enterprise businesses, it’s crucial to have a solid Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system in place. An Enterprise CRM should be able to obtain real-time customer data and easily share that information with employees working with potential and existing clientele—this includes everyone in sales to those in the help desk department.

Even large companies have many options, such as either going premise or cloud-based, when it comes to choosing a CRM solution. In this guide, you will learn about the top Enterprise CRM vendors and their offerings. Many include key features such as built in analytics, customer support module, and multiple hosting options.
Title: CRM for Enterprise Comparison Guide 2016

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
When considering a voice over internet protocol (VoIP) phone system, most businesses choose premise-based, since many find cloud-based VoIP technology a bit daunting and unreliable compared to the legacy phone system.

In this white paper, Ziff Davis contributing writer Jon Arnold explains how the decision to adopt hosted VoIP will trigger a series of implications that will be good for your business and also change the way you think about the strategic value of communications technologies.
Title: Five Implications that make Hosted VoIP Good for your Business

Author: IBM
Summary: BM ECM solutions help organizations digitize and classify paper documents, automate key HR processes, integrate ERP and HRMS environments, introduce an efficient case-management approach, implement electronic forms, conduct content analytics and improve information lifecycle governance.
Title: Optimizing Critical Human Resources Processes

Author: IBM
Summary: HR organizations around the world leverage the IBM ECM platform to manage content and processes associated with the employee lifecycle; promote efficient, consistent and accurate interaction and collaboration; and provide a unified view of structured and unstructured employee information.
Title: Human Capital Management

Author: Dell
Summary:
Enterprise storage requirements are exploding as Big Data applications, increased mobile device usage and industry data retention regulations create a perfect storm of demand. This massive growth in data storage requirements has been going on for several years, and it looks set to continue for several more: Research firm IDC says that enterprise storage capacity has seen a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 53 percent since 2011 and predicts it will continue to grow at a similar rate at least until 2016.

There are many reasons for this growth, but the rise in Big Data applications is probably the most significant one. This whitepaper will further discuss the fast changing economics of flash.
Title: Redefining the Economics of Storage: Flash at the Price of Disk

Author: Dell
Summary: A growing number of organizations are deploying solid-state storage solutions because they provide faster access to data while taking up less space and using less power than a traditional disk-based storage solution. In fact, ESG research has found that the percentage of respondent enterprise organizations that reported leveraging solid-state storage technology has more than doubled between 2008 and 2012. While more than a third of organizations are leveraging the technology in some form, 54% are in various stages of potential adoption: 17% plan on deploying the technology within the next year, 19% are currently evaluating the technology, and 18% are familiar with and interested in the technology.
Title: Changing the Economics of Storage with Compellent Flash Optimized Solutions

Author: IBM
Summary:
Everyone is talking about how using social technologies is important for building successful relationships and for realizing better business outcomes, but what is the best way to get your organization on the path to becoming a social business? Many companies are looking to the cloud to help accelerate the pace of social adoption and to help their employees work more effectively and collaborate across business boundaries.

Employing social cloud technologies can help your company respond more rapidly to market opportunities and to address potential issues as they arise. But for social technology to transform the organization, your employees need to embrace it and to understand the impact these technologies can have on their day-to-day workload and business processes. Cloud services need to be easy to understand and use so employees can act quickly to locate relevant information and expertise from anywhere, anytime.

Join this webinar to learn how:
  • Adopting social cloud capabilities can lead to more rapid innovation and improved ways of doing business.
  • The cloud can help your business cost-effectively extend social collaboration with clients, partners and vendors.
  • You can quickly realize significant business benefits when these tools are applied to business processes.
  • Becoming a social business in the cloud can enhance employee engagement and improve productivity.
Title: Adopt Social Cloud Capabilities to Drive Rapid Innovation and Accelerate Time-to-Value for Your Business

Author: IBM
Summary:
Businesses move from liking to leading when they look beyond social media to see how social technologies drive real business value. From marketing and sales to product and service innovation, social is changing the way people connect and the way organizations succeed.

When you inspire your workforce to innovate and collaborate more productively, you create tangible business value. When you integrate your business processes with the right social tools, you secure a competitive advantage and pioneer new ways of doing business.

Learn how IBM Connections empowers employees and provides the foundation for becoming a successful social business.
Title: Win in Your Marketplace - Becoming a Successful Social Business

Author: IBM
Summary: In this On-Demand session, learn about using cloud-based social collaboration tools to streamline key areas of your business, increasing time to invest in new product development. Hear How one manufacturer turned to an IBM Business.
Title: How Adopting Social Cloud Technologies Speeds Time to Market and Supplier Collaboration for Manufacturers

Author: IBM
Summary:
BYOD (Bring Your Own Device) is not just a trend anymore, it's becoming a reality for today's successful organizations. The growing mobile workforce expects to connect to the corporate network anytime, anywhere, using the mobile device of their choice. And as more and more companies start to adopt social business technologies they are finding that leveraging cloud and mobile together can help them work more efficiently.

In this webcast, you will learn :
  • How moving to the cloud can help accelerate mobile adoption in your organization.
  • The benefits of combining the power of cloud with the freedom and functionality of mobile.
  • Best practices for starting your mobile cloud journey from a client who has made the move.
Title: Give Your Users What They Want with Cloud and Mobile

Author: IBM
Summary:
Is email still the “killer app” it used to be? Social technologies and mobile capabilities are changing the way people communicate in the workplace. Many organizations are employing BYOD strategies and embracing social business tools like file sharing, chat, wikis and communities.

In the past, email was used for storing and sharing documents and having conversations with groups. Tasks which are much better suited for today's social cloud collaboration tools. Email usage may be evolving, but email is not dead. In fact, everyone in the organization from executives to factory workers needs email to stay connected. And many organizations are moving their messaging to cloud to take advantage of the flexibility and cost savings a cloud environment provides.

In this webcast, you will learn:
  • How the nature of email has changed and why everyone in your organization needs it.
  • Why the cloud makes sense for messaging for everyone from executives, to sales, to boundary workers, either as hybrid solution or for the entire workforce.
  • How email complements social business technologies and how you can start using your email more efficiently in the workplace.
  • How moving messaging to the cloud can help reduce IT cost and complexity.
Title: The Evolving Role of Email in the Social Workplace

Author: IBM
Summary:
Advanced analytics strategies yield the greatest benefits in terms of improving patient and business outcomes when applied across the entire healthcare ecosystem. But the challenge of collaborating across organizational boundaries in order to share information and insights is daunting to many stakeholders.

In this worldwide survey of 555 healthcare providers, payers and life sciences organizations, you will learn the importance of implementing collaborative analytics strategies that:
  • Manage, integrate and interpret data generated at all stages of the healthcare value chain.
  • Achieve the right balance of skills in order to translate data into actionable insights.
  • Focus on executive sponsorship and enterprise-wide adoption with metrics to measure and track success.
Position yourself to harness data, create and share insights, make informed decisions, and improve the performance of the entire healthcare ecosystem in which you operate.
Title: Analytics Across the Ecosystem: A Prescription for Optimizing Healthcare Solutions

Author: IBM
Summary: The global healthcare industry is at a pivotal point to transform, reinvent and realign to a more vital and evolving new model. There is broad recognition that cost increases are unsustainable, yet results remain inadequate. Buyers of care, including governments, employers and individual consumers, are demanding better performance in both quality and outcomes. For organizations to adapt, they must have good visibility into their own cost structures and capacities; it requires insight to both financial and clinical risk inherent in their populations, and it will require the ability to measure the impact of their services delivered. This white paper provides an understanding of the key enablers to delivering greater value and achieving real outcomes that matter.
Title: From Evidence to Insights: Achieving Outcomes That Matter

Author: IBM
Summary: Healthcare organizations around the world are challenged by pressures to reduce costs, improve coordination and outcomes, provide more with less and be more patient-centric. Yet, at the same time, evidence is mounting that the industry is increasingly challenged by entrenched inefficiencies and suboptimal clinical outcomes. Read this paper to learn how building analytics competency can help these organizations harness Big Data to create actionable insights, set their future vision, improve outcomes and reduce time to value.
Title: The Value of Analytics in Healthcare: From insights to outcomes

Author: IBM
Summary: Customer Profitability Analytics enables banks to analyze customer, account, product, and transaction data and apply costing models to determine a bank-wide view of profitability. Applying predictive analytics, they can model future behavior and derive a lifetime value for each customer.
Title: How Banks Can Use Customer Profitability Analytics to Thrive in Uncertain Times

Author: IBM
Summary: “Big data”– which admittedly means many things to many people – is no longer confined to the realm of technology. Today it is a business imperative and is providing solutions to long-standing business challenges for banking and financial markets companies around the world. Financial services firms are leveraging big data to transform their processes, their organizations and soon, the entire industry.
Title: The Real-World Use of Big Data in Financial Services: How innovative banking and financial markets organizations extract value from uncertain data

Author: IBM
Summary: This white paper provides insights into the current threat landscape for the financial services industry. Information is based on cyber security event data collected by IBM, as well as data derived from responding to, and performing forensics on, cyber security incidents.
Title: IBM Security Services cyber security intelligence index for financial services

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
It's convenient for today's workforce to educate and be educated through cloud-based virtual training solutions. Virtual training also allows training managers to set up classroom environments quickly, easily, and securely using the latest online tools and strategies.

Download this guide for a side-by-side comparison of the top 10 virtual training vendors based on the 10 most common features and functions.
Title: Virtual Training Comparison Guide

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Unified Communications (UC) is one of the hottest topics for businesses looking to adopt the latest technologies, but also one of the most difficult to understand. While most businesses intuitively understand the basic concept and why it has value, there is no universal definition of it.

This white paper provides a high-level introduction to UC as well as an analysis focused on the bigger picture from our ongoing research on the subject, which you’ll need to better understand why UC is gaining popularity in adoption now. Our findings here will also help set the right expectations for what UC can deliver, along with what you need to do for making good buying decisions while researching UC solutions for your business.
Title: Introduction to Unified Communications

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Many thousands of businesses still use Nortel phone systems and the time is soon coming when this will no longer be viable. Some systems will pass on through attrition, but others will become problems-in-waiting once all forms of support cease in 2015.

This whitepaper examines three distinct options for “Life after Nortel,” and choosing one of these sets the stage for your migration roadmap. It also lays out guidelines for matching the right vendors and solutions for your business as well as providing a five point checklist. These tools were developed from our ongoing research of VoIP trends and how SMBs deploy technology.
Title: Life After Nortel: SMB Migration Roadmap and Buying Decision Checklist

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary: Unified Communications (UC) enables people to collaborate more effectively no matter what tools they use. But the sheer number of potential UC vendors can be overwhelming. This guide compares the prices and features of 2016’s top 10 UC systems.
Title: Unified Communications Comparison Guide

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Webinars are an effective tool for companies to share information such as presentations, seminars, and demonstrations to a broad audience regardless of their physical location.

Recently updated for 2015, this side-by-side comparison lists the top 10 webinar platforms based on the most common features and functionality. All vendors mentioned include both Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) and public switched telephone network (PSTN) integration.
Title: Webinar Solutions Comparison Guide

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Human Capital Management (HCM) solutions are an excellent way to increase performance and reduce costs by automating many HR processes including recruitment, retention, and management.

This side-by-side comparison guide provides a high level view of the top 10 solution providers and based on 10 essential HCM features and functionalities.
Title: Human Capital Management Comparison Guide

Author: Alessandro (Ale) Campioli, IBM Smarter Process Center of Competency, Worldwide Leader
Summary: Business Process Management and Decision Management require an outcome-based approach to maximize the benefit within the enterprise. There are key principles that are fundamental for building success, and this webinar will explain and address each one of them.
Title: Building Success with IBM Smarter Process

Summary: This interactive menu contains an overview and demonstration videos as well as links to additional resources for the IBM SmartCloud Orchestrator solution.
Title: SmartCloud Orchestrator Launchpad

Summary: This infographic illustrates the key functionality of IBM SmartCloud Orchestrator including the three tiers that make up SCO as well as it's key benefits.
Title: Simplify and Accelerate Service Delivery with SmartCloud Orchestrator: Cloud Management for your IT Services

Author: IBM
Summary: This EMA™ research report examines how small, medium, and large enterprises across industries have implemented private cloud technologies to deliver business value.
Title: EMA Research Report: Demystifying Cloud

Author: IBM
Summary: IBM delivers automation and centralized management for a virtualized or cloud environment - and extends those capabilities across virtual and physical machines to cloud-based business services that are managed, optimized and scaled based on demand and policy.
Title: Deploy a dynamic, services-oriented cloud for your business

Author: IBM
Summary: This white paper discusses the emergence of big data analytics as a transformational technology in the management of both facilities and enterprise assets. Through a series of use case examples the white paper presents applications of IBM's big data to in asset and facilities management.
Title: Harness the value of big data to build smarter infrastructures

Author: IBM
Summary:
Create smarter buildings by integrating critical facilities management processes. This buyer’s guide outlines the features and capabilities of an effective facilities management solution, addressing the following key areas:
  1. Facilities space management
  2. Strategic facilities planning
  3. Move management
  4. Workplace reservation management
  5. Management system architecture
Title: Select the right solution for facilities management

Author: IBM
Summary: Data analytics comes in three principal flavors: descriptive, predictive and prescriptive. The first step in using analytics to transform facilities and asset management is to understand the differences so you can make the most of the capabilities they enable and the value they offer.
Title: Descriptive, Predictive, Prescriptive: Transforming facilities and asset management with analytics

Author: ESG
Summary:
Although solid-state in various forms has been a specialist storage technology since the late 1970s, it shed its “niche” moniker for good in 2008. Enterprise-ready flash—fast, not astronomically expensive, and versatile—had arrived, and its maturation allowed storage vendors to begin packaging the technology in ways that could directly improve not only their customers’ IT efficiency, but also their business effectiveness.

In this whitepaper, you will learn how this high-speed storage technology has tremendous potential to support I/O-intensive and/or latency-sensitive applications. Discover how a well-chosen, well-implemented flash-based system can have positive effects such as faster response times, lower TCO, smaller data center footprint, or speedier or more frequent application updating.
Title: ESG: The IBM FlashSystem 840: Technical Evolution to Deliver Business Value

Author: IBM
Summary:
Dominate trends in IT today such as Cloud, Mobile and Smarter Physical Infrastructures are generating massive amount of corporate data. The inherent value of this data coupled with the increasing complexity of IT environments is forcing those tasked with data protection to re-evaluate their approaches.

View this webinar to understand how you can reduce the cost and complexity of backup and recovery while ensuring comprehensive data protection across virtual environments, core application and remote sites.
Title: Reduce the Cost & Complexity of Backup & Recovery

Author: IBM
Summary:
Find out how forward-thinking enterprises are leveraging SaaS (Software as a Service) to propel their businesses forward. Hear the results of new research from the IBM Center for Applied Insights and a global survey of over 800 Business and IT decision makers driving SaaS and Cloud adoption decisions. The study uncovered that over 80 percent of respondents embrace SaaS to enhance the customer experience, enable more strategic business decisions, and accelerate internal and external collaboration.

Learn how leading companies are using SaaS as a competitive advantage across the enterprise. Steve Rogers, Director of the IBM Center for Applied Insights, talks with Craig Hayman, General Manager for IBM Software Industry Solutions, about how companies are using Software as a Service for better decision making, increased collaboration, and market-focused agility.

Summary: Based on a global survey of more than 800 business and IT decision makers who use software as a service (SaaS), this IBM Center for Applied Insights study explores how forward-thinking organizations employ SaaS as a key enabler of business success, not simply as an efficient deployment model. It probes both motivations for adoption as well as business outcomes achieved, examining how these organizations manage their services more strategically and collaboratively.
Title: Champions of Software as a Service

Author: IBM
Summary: The IBM Global SaaS Study highlights the Pacesetter segment - roughy 19% of the survey population - who exhibit the highest level of SaaS adoption and are gaining competitive advantage through their broad efforts.

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary:
Much of the retail sector growth over the next decade will be driven by the Internet; and any business without an e-business strategy loses the chance to connect with buyers looking to interact with a company on their preferred online, mobile or social platform.

Read on to see how leading names like Wen's Wearhouse and Tommy Bahama are harnessing the power of CRM in this competitive and customer-focused industry - and see which solutions they find best-suited for the job.

Author: IBM
Summary: Different types of data have different data retention requirements. In establishing information governance and database archiving policies, take a holistic approach by understanding where the data exists, classifying the data, and archiving the data. IBM InfoSphere Optim™ Archive solution can help enterprises manage and support data retention policies by archiving historical data and storing that data in its original business context, all while controlling growing data volumes and improving application performance. This approach helps support long-term data retention by archiving data in a way that allows it to be accessed independently of the original application.
Title: Business Driven Governance: Managing Policies for Data Retention

Author: IBM
Summary: Information governance establishes and enacts policies for quality, privacy, security and retention of data assets. Read this paper and learn how successful organizations can enable information governance by deploying a strategic information infrastructure, such as Gartner’s ICF principles
Title: Make Your Information Infrastructure Governance-Ready

Author: IBM
Summary: Information integration and governance solutions must become a natural part of big data projects. As the foundation of the IBM big data platform, IBM® InfoSphere® Optim™ provides market-leading functionality across all the capabilities of information integration and governance, including a comprehensive range of capabilities enabling companies to properly manage big data and implement best practices for enterprise-scale data lifecycle management.
Title: The fundamentals of data lifecycle management in the era of big data

Author: IBM
Summary: To help enterprises create trusted insight as the volume, velocity and variety of data continue to explode, IBM offers several solutions designed to help organizations uncover previously unavailable insights and use them to support and inform decisions across the business. Combining the power of IBM® InfoSphere® Master Data Management (MDM) with the IBM big data portfolio creates a valuable connection: big data technology can supply insights to MDM, and MDM can supply master data definitions to big data.
Title: The MDM advantage: Creating insight from big data

Author: ZD B2B A
Summary:
In-memory technology - in which entire data sets are pre-loaded into a computer's random access memory, alleviating the need for shuttling data between memory and disk storage every time a query is initiated - has actually been around for a number of years.

However, with the onset of big data, as well as an insatiable thirst for analytics, the industry is taking a second look at this promising approach to speeding up data processing.
Title: Delivering Information Faster: In-Memory Technology Reboots the Big Data Analytics World

Author: Ziff Davis
Summary: Companies of all sizes are still using analog PBX phone systems even though support will be ending over the next few years. This guide reviews features for IP PBX phone systems side by side, helping you make an intelligent transition to cloud-based phone systems.
Title: IP PBX Comparison Guide

Author: IBM
Summary: In our fast-moving global world, the gap between supply chain leaders and laggards is growing more pronounced. With the IBM Smarter Commerce™ approach of putting the customer at the center of all buy, market, sell and service functions, supply chain leaders are making strides in answering key challenges of minimizing cost and risk and adapting to demand variability. They are tightening collaboration with their peers across the value chain to better serve the new boss—the chief executive customer.

Summary: Today's complex global supply chains are full of uncertainty. The volatile economic environment and customer demand variability require supply chains to able to anticipate, control, and react to disruptions and volatility, in colaboration with customers, suppliers, and logistics partners. In order to restore supply chain stability, companies are looking for ways to optimize their global supply chain operations to execute on a customer value strategy of selling and fulfilling the right products and services, at the right place and time.

Summary: The delivery of an exceptional customer experience is critical to an organization’s long-term success . Strong customer relationships drive revenues, future bookings, and new business.
Title: Exceptional Customer Experience: The New Supply Chain Management Focus

Summary: This Magic Quadrant evaluates vendors providing applications that support the management of marketing resources, such as plans, people, budgets, projects, assets and cycle times. Companies seeking an MRM solution to help manage their marketing resources should review this research.
Title: Magic Quadrant for Marketing Resource Management

Author: IBM
Summary: With every day that passes, it seems that we’re introduced to yet another mobile device or new social network or must-have mobile app. Welcome to the digital lifestyle. Your price of admission, though, isn’t inexpensive. You’re connected, always on, and that’s OK.
Title: The Connected Consumer and the New Decision-Making Cycle

Summary: To understand the impact of marketing management on business outcomes, IBM surveyed more than 500 professionals across fifteen industries. We linked responses to public financial information to see correlation between marketing sophistication and financial performance.

Author: IBM
Summary: Personalization is on the rise as companies strive to meet customer expectations for a more customized and relevant experience. When used effectively, the rewards of personalization can be enormous—increasing sales and revenue, and enhancing online conversion rates.
Title: The Who, What, Where, When and How of Real-time Personalization

Summary: Virgin Atlantic implemented IBM® Digital Analytics software. By aggregating historical and current usage data, it can compare sales performance before and after design changes to the e-commerce site.
Title: Virgin Atlantic Customer Case Study
